title: Scaling: Default graph (6 × 8)
html:
Scaling: Default graph (6 × 8)

Question: On a default idea graph, how does what each society achieves grow with its budget (75 to 9600)?

Answer: At budget 75: best OSO (α = 0.2, β = 1). Against traditional, clearly better on hardest level, knowledge found (bits) and knowledge per unit of money; no clear difference on targets solved, bounty value, ROI and waste. At budget 150: best OSO (α = 0.2, β = 1). Against traditional, clearly better on hardest level, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money and waste; no clear difference on targets solved, bounty value and ROI. At budget 300: best OSO (α = 0.2, β = 1). Against traditional, clearly better on hardest level, targets solved, bounty value, ROI, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money and waste. At budget 600: best OSO (α = 0.8, β = 1). Against traditional, clearly better on hardest level, targets solved, bounty value, ROI, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money and waste. At budget 1200: best OSO (α = 0.8, β = 1). Against traditional, clearly better on hardest level, targets solved, bounty value, ROI, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money and waste; no clear difference on money to the main level. At budget 2400: best OSO (α = 0.8, β = 1). Against traditional, clearly better on targets solved, bounty value, ROI, knowledge per unit of money, money to the main level and waste; no clear difference on hardest level and knowledge found (bits). At budget 4800: best OSO (α = 0.2, β = 1). Against traditional, clearly better on ROI, knowledge per unit of money, money to the main level and waste; no clear difference on hardest level, targets solved, bounty value and knowledge found (bits). At budget 9600: best OSO (α = 0.8, β = 1). Against traditional, clearly better on ROI, knowledge per unit of money, money to the main level and waste; no clear difference on hardest level, targets solved, bounty value and knowledge found (bits). (Compared at each budget; 8 measures, a clear difference is more than 2.7 standard errors.)

  • Budget 75: hardest level: 2.90 against traditional 0.00, clearly better. targets solved: 0.00 against traditional 0.00, no clear difference.
  • Budget 150: hardest level: 4.50 against traditional 0.00, clearly better. targets solved: 0.07 against traditional 0.00, no clear difference.

Design (fixed before the run): compared five societies × budgets 75, 150, 300, 600, 1200, 2400, 4800, 9600 · held the same: a generated idea graph (6 levels × 8 ideas, 2 parents each, sequences of 3 bits growing by 2 per level, composition 0.7), 12 identical agents, budget 75 split equally, no mint, no validation · measure: all of hardest level, targets solved, bounty value, ROI, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money, money to the main level, waste · 30 runs per row.

Caveats:

  • A simulation with guessed parameters: it shows how the rules play out, not that they work.
Details

The simple model on a generated idea graph (6 levels × 8 ideas, 2 parents each, sequences of 3 bits growing by 2 per level, composition 0.7); each run draws its own graph. Only α and β vary. Held fixed: 12 identical agents, a budget of 75 split equally every round (f = 0), no flat mint, a knowledge reward of 1 per new bit flowing back with α, no validation.

Values are mean ± standard deviation over runs.
